title: GuestLinearMemoryBudget
description: Language-neutral linear-memory budget every Semio plugin component is linked and admitted under. `maximumBytes` is the wasm memory `maximum` the component's core module declares (`wasm-ld --max-memory`, set uniformly for `wasm32-wasip2` in `.cargo/config.toml`); `stackBytes` is the shadow stack carved out of it (`wasm-ld -zstack-size`, passed by the dev plugin build in `🧑‍💻dev/📦️packages/🟦️typescript/📜️script.ts`); `installPeakPercent` is the share of `maximumBytes` the boot + contributions-install + first-mesh sequence may peak at before a law fails, so a growing extension closure is caught while headroom still exists rather than as a `rust_oom` trap in a browser tab; `contiguousRequestCeilingBytes` bounds the size of any single block a routine per-command or per-turn path may ask that memory for.

maximumBytes.description: Largest linear memory a plugin guest may grow to, in bytes — 512 MiB, the `maximum` in the component core module's memory section.

stackBytes.description: Shadow stack reserved inside the guest's linear memory, in bytes.

installPeakPercent.description: Share of `maximumBytes`, in percent, the boot + contributions-install + first-mesh sequence's retained-heap peak must stay under.

contiguousRequestCeilingBytes.description: Largest contiguous block, in bytes, a routine per-command or per-turn guest path may request — one wasm page, the guest allocator's growth granularity. A larger request needs a pre-existing large free chunk or a multi-page grow, so it is the first request a fragmented or nearly-full guest refuses.

hostAnswerCeilingBytes.description: Largest ASSEMBLED answer, in bytes, the host may deliver into a guest for one outstanding request — the total an extension result, blob or stream may reach once its `contiguousRequestCeilingBytes` pages are joined. The pages bound what one lowering asks the guest allocator for; this bounds what the assembled buffer may grow to before the guest answers the request with a typed fault instead of allocating further.
